The club will compete in [[Serie B]], following relegation from [[2025–26 Serie A|Serie A]].{{Cite web |title=Eurosport is not available in your region |url=https://www.eurosport.it/geoblocking.shtml |access-date=2025-05-06 |website=www.eurosport.it}}{{Cite web |date=2025-05-06 |title=Official: Pisa join Sassuolo with promotion to Serie A after 34 years |url=https://onefootball.com/it/notizie/official-pisa-join-sassuolo-with-promotion-to-serie-a-after-34-years-41064119 |access-date=2025-05-06 |website=OneFootball |language=it}} The club was founded in 1909 as '''Pisa Sporting Club''' and refounded in 1994 as '''Pisa Calcio''' (and registered in ''Eccellenza'', the regional football division in Italy), after the partial liquidation of the former because of economical troubles. Pisa was excluded again from Italian football in 2009, after failing to collect enough money to service the club's debts.{{cite news|url=http://www.pisacalcio.it/news/dettaglio.html?iId=3166 |publisher=Pisa Calcio |language=it |access-date=10 July 2009 |date=10 July 2009 |title=COMUNICATO UFFICIO STAMPA PISA CALCIO |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090713180413/http://www.pisacalcio.it/news/dettaglio.html?iId=3166 |archive-date=13 July 2009 }} In summer 2009 it was re-founded as '''A.C. Pisa 1909'''. Pisa won two [[Mitropa Cup]]s, in 1986 and 1988. They play their home matches at [[Arena Garibaldi – Stadio Romeo Anconetani]], named after [[Romeo Anconetani]], the chairman who brought and led the club in Serie A during the 1980s. In 2016, Giuseppe Corrado bought the club and planned the new Pisa stadium. In January 2021, billionaire [[Alexander Knaster]] acquired a 75% stake in the available shares of the club.{{Cite web|url=http://www.insideworldfootball.com/2021/01/25/serie-bs-pisa-latest-italian-club-move-foreign-ownership/|title = Serie B's Pisa is latest Italian club to move into foreign ownership|date = 25 January 2021}}"}}
